StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldScaleInMultiplayer.rationale: Multiplayer-only scaling (MultiplayerScalingModel). Out of scope everywhere; the sim is single-player.

AfterSideTurnStart.issue: SLOT, and the sim already has the right one. AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnStart is dispatched by Hook.AfterSideTurnStart at CombatManager.cs:522, i.e. AFTER the player's hand draw; the sim's on_player_turn_start is fired at player.py:169, BEFORE the draw at player.py:183, and the post-draw slot on_player_turn_started (player.py:186 -- whose own comment says it is "the game's AfterPlayerTurnStart / player-side AfterSideTurnStart, both of which run after the draw") is available and unused. Identical shape to the already-recorded demon_form / crimson_mantle / inferno finding (power report section 4 item 6) and to the section-5 slot table. The block here lands on ENEMIES, so the pre/post-draw half of this is dormant on its own -- nothing the player draws can read a Turret Operator's block before it plays -- but see the extra-turn guard below, which makes this unit's rollup LIVE. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.issue: LIVE, and absent from the sim entirely. C# refuses to grant the block on a player's EXTRA turn: _playersTakingExtraTurn is filled at CombatManager.cs:1366-1369 during the side switch and read at :435/:439 inside StartTurn, so it is non-empty when Hook.AfterSideTurnStart fires at :522 for that turn. The sim's extra-turn path (combat.py:648-652) calls `self.player.start_turn()` with no such flag, so on_player_turn_start fires normally and this power grants its block again. EXECUTED: a TURRET_OPERATOR_WEAK combat (enemies [LivingShield(rampart), TurretOperator]) with the ported relic Pael's Eye -- the Turret Operator holds 25 block after the turn-1 start (control, correct in both models); zero it, end the turn WITHOUT playing a card so Pael's Eye claims the extra turn (relics/paels_eye.py:36-40 should_take_extra_turn), and the sim leaves the Turret Operator on 25 block where the game leaves it on 0. Rule-6 co-occurrence, stated explicitly: Pael's Eye comes from the ported Act-2 (Hive) Ancient Pael (events/pael.py:53, OPTION_POOL_3) and Living Shield/Turret Operator is a ported Act-3 (Glory) weak encounter (monsters/glory/turret_operator.py:112-114, monsters/glory/__init__.py:60), and relics persist across acts -- so one run can trivially hold both. Reproduce the extra-turn population with `py tools/audit/power_slot_probes.py extra-turns`. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: Implicit: the sim's on_player_turn_start is only ever fired for the player (player.py:169). Worth noting that this power's OWNER is an enemy while the hook it listens on is the PLAYER's side start -- the one case in this batch where the C# side filter is not an owner filter.

guards.issue: powers.py:3000-3002 adds `and not enemy.is_gone` (recurring gap shape 8, a guard the sim ADDS). C#'s CombatState.Enemies is the raw participant list and a corpse the combat retained is still in it, so the game grants block to a dead-but-present Turret Operator and the sim does not. DORMANT: TurretOperator overrides no ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath, so a dead one leaves the list; and granting block to a corpse is unobservable unless it is later revived. Trigger: a Turret Operator with Illusion/Reattach/Adaptable, or an Osty-style revive.
